text: to create awareness among stakeholders. 25 Aug, 2026 - 25 Aug, 2026 View More Seminars The Bureau of Indian Standards (BIS) is organizing a National Seminar on “Standards in Strengthening Medical Device Quality Ecosystem – Manufacturing, Regulation and Procurement” on 19 August 2026 at BIS Headquarters, New Delhi. The seminar is being organized in line with the mandate of BIS to promote standardization, quality assurance, and stakeholder participation in the development and implementation of Indian Standards. The medical device sector is a critical component of the healthcare ecosystem, where adherence to well-defined technical specifications and quality benchmarks is essential to ensure the safety, performance, reliability, and regulatory compliance of medical devices. title: Standards of the Week | BIS
text: Standards of the Week Archive IS 302 (Part 2/Sec 54): 2026 / IEC 60335-2-54: 2022 Household and Similar Electrical Appliances — Safety, Part 2: Particular Requirements, Section 54: Surface-Cleaning Appliances for Household Use Employing Liquids or Steam This Indian Standard specifies particular safety requirements for household electric surface-cleaning appliances that use liquid cleansing agents or steam, having a rated voltage not exceeding 250 V, including DC-supplied and battery-operated appliances. It also covers wallpaper strippers and cleaning appliances with heating elements or pressurizing means. It is used together with IS 302 (Part 1):2024 (General Requirements) and does not apply to floor treatment/wet scrubbing machines, fixed appliances, high-pressure/steam cleaners under IEC 60335-2-79, commercial appliances, or fabric steamers. It requires appliances to be classified as class I, II or III, with class I/II hand-held liquid-dispensing appliances rated at least IPX7. Appliances must be marked with rated power input, maximum water pressure where applicable, and scalding/hot-surface warning symbols for steam cleaners, wallpaper strippers or liquid dispensers exceeding 50 °C. Table 101 sets maximum permissible temperature rises for accessible external surfaces — bare metal, coated metal, glass/ceramic and plastic — under normal operation, with allowances near air outlets and adjacent surfaces. New tests address current-carrying hoses for resistance to crushing, abrasion, flexing, torsion and low-temperature cracking, each followed by an electric-strength check. Pressurised appliances and instantaneous steam cleaners must incorporate safeguards against excessive pressure, verified through defined over-pressure tests, and switches must prevent inadvertent operation. Mechanical-strength provisions include drop tests for hand-held and body-carried appliances.

title: FAQ | BIS
text: Frequently Asked Questions (FAQs) The Bureau of Indian Standards (BIS) FAQ provides detailed information about BIS's functions, standards formulation, certification processes, quality control, and consumer protection. It answers common queries regarding obtaining BIS certification, understanding product standards, compliance requirements, and accessing BIS services, ensuring clarity and guidance for businesses and consumers alike. What is Standard? A standard is a document that provides agreed solutions to recurring problems. These could be specifications, procedures and guidelines to ensure that products, services and systems are safe, consistent and reliable. Why do we need Standard? Standards help us in many ways. They can:Facilitate trade and commerceImprove processes and make them more efficientGuide in consistent functioning and qualitySimplify comparison of products & servicesEnsure health and safetyConserve resources and reduce impact on our environmentPromote technological developments. How are Standards made? Standards are developed by technical committees of Standards Developing Organizations, that comprises of stakeholders such as manufacturer, consumer, R&D; and scientific institutions, academia, Govt. departments/ Ministries, Regulators and testing laboratories. The nominated experts of such organizations develop standards based on proposals received from any stakeholder following process and practices of good standardization through a process of consensus building aimed at arriving at a common stand point. What is Indian Standard? As per the BIS Act 2016, standard that is established and published by BIS (the National Standards Body) in relation to any good, process, system or service is an Indian Standard. Are there other bodies apart from BIS that develop standards in India? There are a few other dedicated standards bodies in India that also develop Standards in their specific domains, such as: Telecom Engineering Centre (TEC) in the telecommunications sector Indian Road Congress (IRC) in the area of roads and bridges Directorate of Standardization, Ministry of Defence for defence standards Research Design and Standards Organization (RDSO) for standardization of railway equipments & applications Automobile Research Association of India (ARAI) for automotive industry standards Telecommunications Standards Development Society, India (TSDSI) for standards on telecom/ICT products & services. There are a few others Ministries/Departments and Regulators who also develop standards for their respective statutory/ regulatory provisions/purposes. These include Food Safety & Standards Authority of India (FSSAI) for standards on food safety Indian Road Congress (IRC) in the area of roads and bridges Central Pollution Control Board [CPCB] for standards on emission or discharge of environmental pollution Atomic Energy Regulatory Board (AERB) for safety requirements & guidance for utilities and users of atomic energy Directorate of Marketing Inspection (DMI) for grading standards of agricultural commodities Central Drugs Standards Control Organization [CDSCO] the standards for drugs and medical devices. How can I get involved in standards development? BIS standards development processes are open to participation by anyone interested. BIS standards development processes are open to participation by anyone interested. Any individual/organization that is interested has different options of participation. These are: By commenting on our published standards and/or draft standards. All published standards and draft standards are accessible on BIS website with a provision to also comment on such document. By proposing a subject for standardization – Any individual/organization can propose a subject for development of a new standard to BIS, on BIS Website By becoming a member of a technical committee - Any organization can express their interest to play an active role in standards development and membership of a technical committee. The request is then considered by the technical committee for co-option, subject to limitations on maintaining balance of representation of all interested groups and a workable size of committees. Are Standards mandatory? Application/ Implementation of all standards are voluntary but may become an obligation/ mandatory requirement when a standard (in part or whole) referenced in a regulation or in procurement processes adopted by public authorities. A standard becomes mandatory also when contractually agreed between two parties. How do I access/ obtain a standard? Do I have to pay for accessing a standard? All Indian standards are accessible and freely downloadable from BIS website, except for Indian Standards that are adoptions of international standards. How do I search for a standard? How do I search for a standard? You can search for an Indian Standard on BIS website using the ‘Search for Standards’ facility by entering a title, key word or Indian Standard number in the Search Box. If I have any query on an Indian Standard or like to have information on a standard, whom do I approach? You can forward all your technical queries to Technical Information Services of BIS at ird@bis.gov.in. In case, you are aware of the concerned technical department of BIS dealing with the standard in question, you can also send your query directly to the department over email. Information about technical department and their contact details are available on BIS website.

These standards address design requirements, engineering integrity, measurement techniques and test procedures. Their purpose is to provide a basis for design, quality assurance and certification. The standards are concerned with all subsystems of wind turbines, such as mechanical and internal electrical systems, support structures and control and protection systems. They are intended to be used together with appropriate Indian Standards. text: Indian Standards for the railways field which includes rolling stock, fixed installations, management systems (including communication, signalling and processing systems) for railway operation, their interfaces and their ecological environment. These standards cover railway networks, metropolitan transport networks (including metros, tramways, trolleybuses and fully automated transport systems) and magnetic levitated transport systems. These standards relate to systems, components and software and they will deal with electrical, electronic and mechanical aspects, the latter being limited to items depending on electrical factors. These standards deal with electromechanical and electronic aspects of power components as well as with electronic hardware and software protocols for achieving compatibility in interface.
